method: Encoding clips latitude to -90 to 90 and normalises longitude to -180 to 180, shifts both into positive ranges and takes the integer quotient at each place value of 20, 1, 0.05 and 0.0025 degrees (and, for ten characters, 0.000125 degrees), mapping 0 to 19 onto the alphabet 23456789CFGHJMPQRVWX; the '+' separator follows the eighth character. The eleventh character refines the last cell with a 5-row by 4-column grid, so it is finer in latitude than in longitude. Decoding reverses the place values and adds the resolution of the last decoded pair, giving the south-west and north-east corners, the centre and the cell size; a short code omits its leading characters and is recovered by prefixing the characters of the reference point at the matching resolution and then shifting one cell when the decoded centre lies more than half a cell away. Latitude 90 is moved a fraction of a cell south before encoding so the code still decodes, and longitude 180 is read as -180. Lengths of 8, 10 and 11 significant characters are accepted; only ten and eleven character codes are shortened, because an eight character code has no spare leading pair to drop. Cell sizes in metres use 111320 m per degree of latitude and the same value scaled by the cosine of the latitude for longitude, so they are approximate. Short-code recovery is exact when the reference lies in the same cell as the original point; a reference across a cell boundary selects the neighbouring full code, as the format intends. Everything runs in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Google Open Location Code specification: a 20-character alphabet (23456789CFGHJMPQRVWX), latitude/longitude pairs at 20, 1, 0.05, 0.0025 and 0.000125 degrees, and a 5 by 4 grid refinement character.
Google Maps Plus Codes documentation: a full code has eight characters before the '+' and up to two after it, while a short code omits leading characters that are recovered from a reference location.
